Tilberede autentiske kinesiske retter med fokus på kvalitet, smag og præsentation.

• 
Gerne taler kinesisk, da det kan være en fordel i den daglige kommunikation og i arbejdet med traditionelle kinesiske opskrifter. Det er dog ikke et krav.

En spændende stilling i en veletableret kinesisk restaurant med stærk lokal forankring.

Siteimprove helps organisations make their digital content accessible to everyone. Our accessibility products scan entire web estates and document libraries, find the barriers that stop people using them, and increasingly fix those barriers automatically. The work is measured in public: our customers are universities, health systems, government agencies and Fortune 500 companies who have legal deadlines to meet and auditors to satisfy.

We are looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to lead one of our two accessibility product teams. You will own the delivery, quality and technical direction of a cross-functional team of engineers working alongside a Product Manager and a Designer, and you will be accountable for what that team ships and for how the people in it grow.

This role sits at a genuine inflection point. We are moving from finding accessibility problems to explaining and fixing them, and we are rebuilding how we develop software around AI agents that write, test and review code under human direction. We need a leader who is credible in the code, fluent in modern AI-assisted development, and able to coach a team through that change without trading away quality or the well-being of the people doing the work.

What we will be doing

• Own delivery for your team. Turn a product roadmap into a sequenced, realistic plan, keep commitments honest, and be the person who says early and clearly when something will not land.

• Lead the people. Hold regular one-to-ones, give direct and useful feedback, run performance and growth conversations, and build a team where engineers at different levels can do their best work. Recruit, onboard and retain.

• Stay hands-on enough to be credible. Read and review code and designs, take part in architectural decisions, and pair with engineers when it helps. You are not expected to carry a full delivery load, but you are expected to understand the system well enough to challenge a design and to know when an estimate is wrong.

• Coach the team in AI-assisted development. Raise the whole team's effectiveness with AI tooling: how to decompose a problem so an agent can take it, how to write a prompt and a specification that produce reviewable work, and how to review agent-generated code properly rather than approving it on sight.

• Set the standards for how AI-generated work is accepted. Define with your engineers how such work is reviewed, tested, secured and documented before it merges, and hold the line that a human is always accountable for what ships.

• Partner with Product and Design as equals. Work with your Product Manager on outcomes, scope and sequencing, and make the technical trade-offs visible so the three of you decide together.

• Work across teams. Depend on and contribute to Platform, AI and other product teams. Much of what your team needs will be built elsewhere, and much of what it builds will be consumed elsewhere.

• Protect engineering health. Hold a deliberate balance between roadmap delivery, compliance obligations, customer-reported defects and technical debt, and make that balance explicit rather than letting it be decided by whatever is loudest.

• Own quality and operational responsibility. Testing, accessibility conformance of our own products, security and vulnerability remediation, incident response and the reliability of what your team runs in production.

• Adjust your working hours to overlap with the United States. This role reports to a manager on the US Pacific coast and partners with colleagues across the US. You will regularly take meetings in the late afternoon or early evening Central European Time, and we will protect the rest of your week in return.

• Travel may be required; a valid passport is required

• Perform other duties as assigned

What we will require of you

• Engineering management experience. Several years leading software engineering teams as their direct manager, including hiring, performance management and developing engineers at more than one level. You have owned delivery for a team over a sustained period, not just a project.

• A real software engineering background. You have built and shipped production software yourself and can still read a pull request, follow a design discussion and form your own view. We will talk about systems you have built.

• Depth in at least one of our core languages, and comfort across the rest. Our services are written mainly in C# and .NET, TypeScript and JavaScript, Go, Rust and Python. You do not need all of them; you do need to be genuinely strong in one and unafraid of the others.

• Modern cloud and delivery practice. AWS, containers and Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, observability and on-call practice.

• Practical use of AI in the software lifecycle. You have personally used AI coding assistants and agents on real work, you know where they help and where they mislead, and you have opinions about how their output should be reviewed. Experience helping other engineers adopt them is what sets this role apart.

• Strong partnership with Product. A track record of working with Product Managers and Designers as a peer, shaping scope rather than receiving it.

• Clear written and spoken English, and the ability to explain a technical trade-off to a non-technical audience.

• Willingness to work a shifted day. Regular overlap with US Pacific time, and occasional travel.

What we will love about you

• Digital accessibility knowledge. Familiarity with WCAG, assistive technology, or the accessibility conformance and reporting that regulated customers require. If you do not have it, you must be willing to learn it properly — it is the product.

• Experience in a compliance or regulated environment, such as FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001 or a public-sector authorisation, and comfort working inside an audited change process.

• Open-source stewardship. We build and maintain an open-source accessibility rules engine, and experience running a public project and its community is valuable.

• Large-scale data or crawling systems, document processing, or machine learning applied to content analysis.

• Experience leading a distributed or multi-site team, including working effectively with contractors and vendor partners.

• Having introduced AI-assisted development to an organisation, including the governance, measurement and change management that goes with it.

• Danish language skills are a nice-to-have and are not required; our working language is English.

What you'll love about us

We’re building the next generation of AI-powered content intelligence, helping organizations unify accessibility, SEO/AEO, analytics, and content performance into one platform. If you’re energized by solving complex problems, working cross-functionally, and contributing to a product with real-world impact, we’d love to connect.

In addition, we hope you will appreciate:

At Siteimprove, we're committed to supporting your wellbeing both at work and beyond. Our Denmark benefits are designed to help you thrive personally and professionally.

Rest and relaxation: Generous time off including Danish holiday entitlements, five additional FF Days, child sick leave, and bereavement leave.

Comprehensive benefits: Health insurance, company-paid mobile phone support, and internet allowance to support your day-to-day needs.

Prepare for the future: Danica pension with employer contributions to help support your retirement goals.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral research in plant regulatory genomics and artificial intelligence
jobs.employer_name: Center for Kvantitativ Genetik og Genomforskning
jobs.description:
The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) at Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for a two-year postdoctoral position in plant regulatory genomics and artificial intelligence, starting 1 April 2027.

You will design new sequence-to-expression deep learning models that predict gene expression from DNA sequence in plants, using new experimental datasets generated in the project. The position includes a 6- to 12-month research stay at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory (CSHL), USA, combining plant genomics expertise at Aarhus with AI expertise at CSHL.

This is an opportunity to advance the state of the art in AI for plant biology while working across two leading research environments. For more information, feel free to reach out to Guillaume Ramstein (QGG) and Peter Koo (CSHL).

Expected start date and duration of employment

This is a 2-year position from April 1st 2027, or as soon as possible.

Job description

You will advance the field of artificial intelligence applied to regulatory genomics, as part of the GRASP project funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark. In this project, you will leverage new training sets, build novel deep learning architectures and define dedicated learning objectives, to learn the effects of genetic variants on gene expression.

The position will focus on data science and genomics in a model plant species, Brachypodium distachyon. You will work at the cutting edge of AI in biology and propose new solutions to predict the effects of regulatory variants in plant genomes, which remains an open research problem in plant genomics. 

These activities will be carried out in close collaboration with the Koo lab, a leading group in AI and regulatory genomics at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory (CSHL), USA. As part of this collaboration, the position will include a 6- to 12-month research stay in the Koo lab.

Your profile

Applicants should hold a PhD in computer science, bioinformatics, or a related field, or expect to complete it before the start date. They should have research experience in deep learning.

Applicants are expected to have published in international peer-reviewed journals, preferably on topics related to AI and genomics. Experience in developing new deep learning techniques (model architectures or learning objectives) is especially relevant to this position. 

Good communication skills in English are required, as well as the ability to work in an interdisciplinary team of AI experts, computational geneticists, and plant biologists.

Who we are

The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) is a major center for research and education in quantitative genetics and genomics at Aarhus University (http://www.qgg.au.dk/en). We conduct basic and applied research in animal, plant, and human genetics. Our focus areas include quantitative genetics, artificial intelligence applied to agriculture and medicine, population genetics, and integrative genomics. Research within QGG is characterized by a very close synergy between method development and application on practical problems across species, in collaboration with industry partners. QGG is an international research center with about 70 employees and visiting researchers from over 15 nations. QGG works in teams and strives for an excellent working environment, in which we value self-leadership, open communication, and commitment to diversity and inclusion.

What we offer

The succesful candidate will be offered:

• A 6- to 12-month research stay in the Koo lab at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory (CSHL), USA, providing international experience and the opportunity to work across two leading labs in plant genomics and AI.
• Computational ressources, including the GenomeDK high-performance computing cluster, with growing capabilities such as high-memory nodes and state-of-the-art GPUs.
• An interdisciplinary interdisciplinary environment, in which the candidate will be able to exchange across research fields (machine learning, bioinformatics, biology, and quantitative genetics) and applications (plant biology, agriculture, and biomedicine).
• A research environment characterized by collaboration, professionalism, commitment to diversity and inclusion, and success in mentoring and supervision.
• A healthy work-life balance.
Place of work and area of employment

The primary place of work is C. F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000, Aarhus (Denmark), and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

The position will also include a 6- to 12-month research stay at 1 Bungtown Rd, Cold Spring Harbor, NY 11724, United States. The time and duration of the research stay may be negotiated with the supervisors Guillaume Ramstein and Peter Koo.

Contact information

For further information, please contact:

• Tenure-Track Assistant Professor Guillaume Ramstein, +45 42 52 12 66, ramstein@qgg.au.dk
• Associate Professor Peter Koo, +1 516 367 5520, koo@cshl.edu
Deadline

Applications must be received no later than November 20th, 2026.

Aarhus Universitet er et fagligt bredt og forskningsintensivt universitet med høj kvalitet i uddannelse og forskning, og et stærkt engagement i samfundsudviklingen nationalt og globalt. jobs.occupation: Senior Frontend Engineer - with an interest in fullstack
jobs.description:
About Cardlay
Cardlay is a Danish fintech building white-label card and spend management solutions. Banks, issuers and financial partners in Europe and the US offer our platform to their business customers using their own brand.

We are a small dedicated team with short decision paths. We make bold decisions, turn them into results by helping each other, and give people the mandate to own what they build.
About the job
Our web portal is where companies run their spend: cards, expenses, accounting and people management. Every bank offers it under its own brand.

Some of the core capabilities include

• Cards: card programs, card orders and requests, and funding accounts
• Expenses: transactions, receipts, mileages and expense policies
• Accounting: categories, cost dimensions, GL accounts and exports to external accounting systems
• People and teams: onboarding, invitations, roles and company settings
Under the hood, it's React, TypeScript, pnpm workspaces and Vite.

Every new bank brings its own brand and requirements, and AI agents now write a growing share of our code. We need a senior engineer who builds the product and keeps the shared components and patterns behind them consistent, so new screens, whether built by people or AI agents, look and work like the rest of the product.

This is a hands-on product role with significant ownership: you will build features every day and help set our frontend direction.

What success looks like after a year

• Customers use features you built and shipped end to end
• A new feature takes less code and fewer review rounds than it does today
• New screens are built from shared components by default, by people and AI agents alike
• The core libraries are up to date with latest security updates and we are on a clear upgrade path going forward
The challenge

Customers rely on the platform every day, and it has grown over several years:

• Some pages use our new design system and some don't yet. Deciding what to migrate, and when, to keep the experience consistent is ongoing work
• You work closely with our UI/UX Lead. That takes the confidence to push back on designs that hurt the user experience, and the taste to know when you're right
• There are several ways of handling data and state in the codebase, and picking the right one for each case directly affects what customers experience
• We're a small team, and other developers contribute a lot to the web portal. As the senior frontend engineer, you decide what's good enough to merge and where our code style and stack go next
• You look beyond your own domain. When the answer is on the other side of the API, you read the backend code and unblock yourself where you canWhat you'll do
As a Senior Frontend Engineer, you will own the frontend of our web portal. You take responsibility for what we ship, make decisions others can build on, drive projects forward and help the people around you grow.

You will be the primary frontend engineer in an engineering team of 10 people across frontend, backend, mobile and DevOps. You will work closely with Product and our UI/UX Lead, and report to our Head of Engineering.

Your responsibilities will include

• Take responsibility for the frontend as a whole: its quality, performance and direction
• Make the key frontend decisions and stand by them: architecture, what goes into the design system and when to say no
• Drive projects from idea to production with Product and our UI/UX Lead, and own them until customers are using them
• Build reusable components and patterns as part of your product work, not one-off solutions
• Move legacy screens onto the design system as you work on them, without silent visual regressions
• Set up component APIs, lint rules and docs so AI agents produce code that fits
• Mentor other engineers and share what you know through reviews, docs and pairingWho you are
We are looking for an experienced frontend engineer who loves building a product and cares about the quality and consistency behind it.

You likely bring

• Deep experience with React and TypeScript
• You have shipped complex features in a web product that customers rely on
• You use AI coding tools every day and know where they go wrong
• A good eye for UX and product quality
• You speak up when something could be done better, and you see your work through to production
• You have driven projects with other engineers and helped them grow through mentoring and reviews
Bonus if you have

• Experience building component libraries or design systems
• Design tokens or white-label theming
• Interest in fullstack work, so you can help out on the backend when you can
• Experience from fintech or complex B2B products
You will work with the technologies below. We don't expect experience with all of them; we are looking for engineers who learn quickly.

• React, TypeScript
• Vite, pnpm workspaces, Biome
• MUI, styled-components, Storybook
• TanStack Query, TanStack Table, Redux Toolkit
• React Hook Form, react-intl
• Vitest, MSW, CypressWhy Cardlay
You will join at a point where our platform is proven, our customer base is growing and AI is changing how we build software. You will have a real say in how Cardlay builds the frontend, in a team where senior engineers set the direction.

• Permanent employment, freelance or consultancy, with salary or rate matching experience
• Hybrid work from our offices in Copenhagen or Odense
• English as our main working language, with Danish spoken too. You don't need to speak Danish to join
• Flexible working hours, and the option to work from home when it suits you and the team
• Company-paid phone and home internet
• Lunch, coffee, fruit, drinks and snacks at the officeHow to apply
Go ahead and hit "apply" and upload your résumé, application and other relevant information through our HR system.

Any questions about the position can be directed to our Head of Engineering:

Magnus Biolzi Hansen, Mail: mbh@cardlay.com, Telephone: +45 42 28 62 42

Application deadline: We review applications as they come in and will close the position once we've found the right person.

We offer an exciting and visible role in a complex international group undergoing transformation.

JOB DESCRIPTION

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

The Role

Genmab is searching for an energized Senior Associate to be part of Global Clinical Supply Manufacturing in Copenhagen within commute distance from our office locations to work according to your hybrid work arrangement.

With an impressive pipeline and many ongoing clinical trials, you will have a central role in supporting inspection readiness across our late-stage clinical development portfolio. Your work will help ensure that documentation is complete, compliant and readily available to support the successful execution of business-critical GMP and GCP inspections.

You will support inspection readiness activities within Global Clinical Supply, collecting, organizing and performing completeness and compliance checks of trial-specific documentation. During inspections, you will participate in back-office activities and help ensure timely retrieval and follow-up of requested information.

The role also offers an opportunity to develop beyond inspection readiness. You will work closely with the Head of Global Clinical Supply Manufacturing and support selected functional initiatives, providing exposure to broader activities across the organization and our CMO and vendor network. In parallel, you will have the opportunity to build your GMP and clinical supply knowledge by learning and supporting selected operational activities related to outsourced packaging and labelling of IMP and AxMP.

The position reports to the Director, Head of Global Clinical Supply Manufacturing based in Copenhagen.

Responsibilities

• Support inspection readiness across late-stage clinical trials by collecting, organizing and maintaining relevant clinical supply documentation.

• Perform completeness and compliance checks of trial-specific documentation against applicable procedures and inspection-readiness expectations.

• Participate in back-office activities during GMP and GCP inspections, including document retrieval, request coordination and tracking of responses and follow-up items.

• Support preparation for mock inspections, audits and health authority inspections, including compilation and review of supporting documentation for completeness and readiness.

• Support the Head of Global Clinical Supply Manufacturing with selected functional initiatives and tasks across the organization.

• Support activities related to our external CMO and vendor network, including coordination, follow-up and preparation of relevant material and documentation.

• Build knowledge of GMP and clinical supply activities within Global Clinical Supply Manufacturing and learn and support selected operational tasks related to outsourced packaging and labelling of IMP and AxMP.

• Participate in maintenance and continuous improvement of procedures, tools and ways of working supporting inspection readiness and clinical supply activities.

• Responsible to be compliant with Genmab´s quality system.

Requirements

• Minimum a bachelor’s degree or equivalent.

• Some experience working with documentation, quality or compliance activities in the pharmaceutical, biotech, clinical research or another regulated environment is an advantage.

• Knowledge and understanding of GMP and GCP; experience with inspection or audit readiness is an advantage.

• Strong interest in documentation, quality and compliance, with a structured and detail-oriented approach to your work.

• Ability to coordinate activities, maintain structure and follow up on actions involving multiple stakeholders.

• Ability to work successfully under pressure in a fast-paced environment and with tight timelines, including during inspections.

• Ability to be proactive, enthusiastic, curious and goal orientated, with a willingness to learn new GMP-related activities.

• A team player with demonstrated ability to work effectively with internal and external stakeholders, including CMOs and vendors.

• Strong communication skills in English - both oral and written.

The Team

You will be part of a highly competent team focused on GMP applicable to packaging and labelling of supplies for clinical trials, with a strong focus on quality, inspection readiness and successful collaboration with our internal stakeholders and CMOs.

Together with Global Clinical Supply Portfolio & Project Delivery and Global Clinical Supply Systems, the teams make up the Global Clinical Supply department.

We have an international and informal working environment with a high pace, strong one-team spirit and close collaboration across functions.

Application

Has this sparked your interest? Then we encourage you to upload your CV and cover letter including your motivation for this position. We screen candidates on a continuous basis and call in for interviews.

Fully remote applicants will not be considered, so please indicate if you are willing to relocate if you’re not currently living in commute distance.

DKK544.000,00---816.000,00

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.
